Maia for Recruiting and staffing

Prepare the handoff while people make the hiring decision.

Maia organizes approved role, candidate, client, and scheduling context into clear team briefs in Slack. Recruiters and hiring teams retain evaluation, selection, compensation, and employment decisions.

All industries ↗

Coordinate the work around a placement

Recruiting and staffing teams manage client requirements, candidate records, interview schedules, feedback, offers, and start dates across several systems. Maia can prepare the administrative handoffs in Slack so the team sees missing information and next owners.

It should not rank candidates or make hiring recommendations. Recruiters, clients, and hiring managers evaluate people and make every employment decision.

Clarify the role intake

Provide the approved job description, client or hiring-manager notes, location, schedule, compensation range where authorized, and intake template. Maia can identify missing requirements, conflicting statements, and questions that need confirmation.

The recruiter resolves those questions before sourcing or presenting candidates. A clean intake brief helps the team use the same role facts without turning preferences into unsupported requirements.

Prepare interview logistics

Using the schedule, panel roles, approved candidate record, and interview plan, Maia can prepare a brief with times, links, responsibilities, accommodations already arranged through the proper process, and missing assignments.

The recruiter approves the candidate communication and keeps private details within the authorized audience. Maia handles coordination, not assessment.

Build a candidate handoff

For a client submission or internal panel handoff, provide the approved candidate profile, verified work history, recruiter notes, and role criteria. Maia can organize factual experience, stated preferences, availability, and open questions.

The recruiter checks every claim and chooses what to share. Sensitive attributes and private notes should stay out of broad channels. The brief must not infer traits, fit, or likelihood of success.

Track offer and start readiness

Once authorized people make a selection, Maia can prepare a checklist for approved offer documents, background or reference steps, equipment, account setup, and first-day logistics. It can surface missing owners and dates.

HR, the employer, and the candidate control the underlying decisions and consents. Keep any proposed status change or document visible for the authorized owner to review.

Start with scheduling

Choose an administrative workflow with a sample role, candidate record, and panel schedule. Include a conflicting time and missing interviewer. Check that Maia resolves neither by guesswork and that no evaluation language appears in the brief.

After each interview round, Maia can prepare an administrative recap with completed sessions, missing feedback forms, scheduling conflicts, and the next communication due. It should not summarize private assessment content into a broad operations channel.

For staffing firms, the same handoff can include the client's confirmed start date, required onboarding records, time-entry instructions, and account owner. Recruiters and client teams review the facts before the worker receives the final schedule.

Open logistics stay assigned to named owners.

Questions from recruiting teams

Does Maia screen or rank candidates?

No. This workflow prepares authorized records and logistics. People evaluate candidates and make selection decisions.

Can Maia use our applicant tracking system?

Confirm the exact connection and operation available. Authorized exports can support a first coordination workflow.

Can Maia contact candidates?

It can draft approved logistical messages. A recruiter verifies the recipient, content, and send, especially when the message affects candidacy or employment terms.
